report:
Your skepticism is well-supported by the evidence.

**Conclusion: The claim is false.** No scientific evidence shows that boiled garlic water can cure, treat, or prevent COVID-19.

**What the evidence shows:**

1. **Official health authorities have explicitly debunked this.** The World Health Organization's COVID-19 "Mythbusters" series states directly: "Garlic is a healthy food that may have some antimicrobial properties. However, there is no evidence from the current outbreak that eating garlic has protected people from the new coronavirus" (https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters). No clinical trials have tested garlic water against COVID-19, and none exist showing it clears the virus, reduces severity, or shortens illness duration.

2. **No specific cure exists for COVID-19 via home remedies.** Fact-checking outlets covering the pandemic uniformly note that no food, drink, or home remedy—including garlic—has been proven to cure the disease, and such claims fall into the broader category of pandemic-era misinformation alongside cow dung, high-dose vitamins, and other unproven treatments (https://www.factchecker.in/experts-call-out-claims-that-cow-dung-urine-yoga-ayush-can-prevent-or-treat-covid-19/).

3. **Belief in the myth caused real harm.** Reports documented a Chinese woman hospitalized with a severely inflamed throat after consuming 1.5 kg of raw garlic trying to prevent infection, and a peer-reviewed case report described a chemical burn on an elderly patient's tongue from excessive garlic use during the pandemic (https://www.bbc.com/news/world-51735367; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8242564/).

**Bottom line:** While garlic has mild, general antimicrobial compounds studied in lab settings, this is far removed from curing an active SARS-CoV-2 infection in humans. The claim is unsupported and potentially dangerous if it delays proper medical care.
